action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

The call ends your run, so do everything else first and put everything your caller needs in that one report. It is not a messaging channel: do not use it for progress updates or questions.

Only a report delivered through SubagentHandback reaches your caller; plain text you write at the end of your run is NOT delivered. There is no recipient parameter: the report can only go to your caller.

entries.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

offset.description: Character position in the page text to start reading from. Use it to read on through a page too long for one call, with the value the previous result gave.

entries.name: WebSearch
entries.description:
Search the web. Returns result blocks with titles and URLs. US-only.

- The current month is (provided in the conversation below) — use this when searching for recent information.
- `allowed_domains` / `blocked_domains` filter results.
- After answering from results, end with a "Sources:" list of the URLs you used as markdown links.

allowed_domains.description: Only include search results from these domains

blocked_domains.description: Never include search results from these domains

mode.description: "standard": the normal web search: quick and cheap; right for straightforward lookups (reference facts, official pages, documentation, well-known people, places and topics) and simple follow-up lookups. "extended": a thorough, fresh search at several times the cost and latency.

BYD's Smart Driving Edition launch took place on February 10, 2025, and the results I found cover the Tang and Song Plus in detail, but not the Qin Plus or Han launch dates.

**The event:** The NEV maker rolled out Smart Driving Edition updates for 21 models on February 10, including the Seagull priced as low as RMB 69,800. Before the event, Lu Tian, head of sales for BYD's Dynasty lineup, said on Weibo that the lineup's six families -- Han, Tang, Qin, Song, Yuan, and Xia -- would see a complete upgrade.

**Tang:** Gasgoo reports that on the evening of February 10, BYD announced the market launch of the Tang DM-i Smart Driving edition at its intelligence strategy launch event. It is available in four trim levels, priced between 179,800 yuan and 219,800 yuan. The entry-level and mid-spec versions provide the God's Eye C smart driving system, while the top-spec variant is equipped with the God's Eye B system.

**Song Plus:** Gasgoo reports that on February 10, BYD's Ocean Series put the Smart Driving editions of its 11 vehicle models onto the market, involving the Seal 05 DM-i, the Song PLUS, the Dolphin, and the Seagull. The Song Plus Smart Driving edition will come with the God's Eye C system (DiPilot 100).

**Qin Plus and Han:** The sources only say the Qin Plus will be upgraded to fifth-generation DM technology and has a new exterior and interior. I found no launch details for the Qin Plus or Han Smart Driving editions, so I can't confirm their pricing or dates from these results.

**God's Eye background:** The company refers to its smart driving systems as God's Eye. The company has dubbed its Smart Driving system as God's Eye, which is split into God's Eye A for ultra-luxury vehicles, God's Eye B for premium vehicles, and God's Eye C for affordable models. Later, CnEVPost reported that as of July 6, the company's Smart Driving Edition models equipped with the God's Eye smart driving systems have surpassed 1 million units in cumulative deliveries.

Sources: [CnEVPost, Feb 10, 2025 preview](https://cnevpost.com/2025/02/10/byd-execs-preview-intelligence-event/), [CnEVPost, 1 million milestone](https://cnevpost.com/2025/07/07/byd-1-million-delivered-smart-driving-edition/), [Gasgoo, Tang DM-i](https://autonews.gasgoo.com/articles/news/byd-puts-tang-dm-i-smart-driving-edition-onto-market-70035946), [Gasgoo, Ocean Series](https://autonews.gasgoo.com/articles/news/smart-driving-editions-of-byd-ocean-series-11-vehicle-models-hit-market-70035944).

The BYD Qin Plus EV 2023 Champion Edition launched on April 7, 2023, with a top trim rated at 610 km of range.

**Launch date:** BYD launched a new version of its Qin Plus EV on Friday, and Carnewschina gives the date as April 7.

**Variants:** China Daily reports that the 2023 champion version, available in six variants, is expected to take on gasoline vehicle rivals. Gizmochina lists the six as the 420km leading model, 420km beyond type, 510km leading model, and 510 km beyond type, plus the 510km excellent type and 610km excellent type models. **Range and performance:** The 610 km figure is the CLTC rating. The model can generate a maximum output of 150 kW and has a driving range up to 610 km on one charge thanks to BYD's blade-shaped batteries. Carnewschina adds that the electric motor's 150 kW output enables it to accelerate from 0 to 100 km/h in 3.8 seconds. Carnewschina's table lists 0–50 km/h in 3.8 s for the 610 km trim, which supports the 0–50 reading.

**Other features:** The car uses the e-platform 3.0, with an eight-in-one powertrain and a BYD LFP blade battery. It supports DC fast charging and can charge from 30% to 80% in 30 minutes. The interior includes an 8.8-inch full LCD panel and the DiLink 4.0 intelligent network connection system.

**Pricing:** Sources disagree. Carnewschina lists the 610 km trim at 176,800 RMB (25,700 USD), while another Carnewschina database page shows the 610km Excellence at 156,800 yuan with a 176,800 yuan launch MSRP. Treat the exact price as unconfirmed.

The Champion Edition's 120 km trim went on sale in China on August 9, 2023, at 119,800 yuan (about 16,700 USD). This is the newest Destroyer 05 Champion Edition launched by Chinese EV manufacturer, BYD. With the launch of this model, there are currently six Champion Edition models on sale, with an official price range of 101,800 – 148,800 yuan (14,100 – 20,600 USD).

**What changed:** The launch was mostly a pricing and configuration update. The design of the new car is consistent with that of the current models, the main changes are the price and configurations.

**Key specs and features:**
- **Powertrain:** The car keeps BYD's DM-i plug-in hybrid setup, with a 1.5L naturally aspirated engine, an electric motor, and an E-CVT gearbox. Its 18.3kWh lithium iron phosphate monolithic battery pack provides a pure electric cruising range of 120 km (NEDC).
- **Total range:** Under a full fuel tank and full charge, the comprehensive cruising range exceeds 1,200 km, BYD claims.
- **Performance:** The official 0 – 100 km/h acceleration time is 7.3 seconds, and the fuel consumption is 4.6L/100km.
- **Charging and power output:** The car supports a 17kW DC fast charging function and a vehicle-to-load feature that supports power up to 3kW, so the car can power household appliances.

**Later variant:** In February 2024, BYD launched a cheaper Honor Edition. Coming with six trim levels, the new product is priced between 79,800 yuan and 128,800 yuan. content.content:
**Launch date:** Fang Cheng Bao launched the Bao 5 Smart Driving Edition variants on February 21, 2025. Deliveries of the BYD God's Eye C versions begin in mid-March, and the Huawei versions in April.

**Smart Driving variants:**
- **Prices:** Four variants start at RMB 239,800 ($33,090), RMB 259,800, RMB 284,800, and RMB 329,800.
- **God's Eye:** The two cheaper variants use BYD's God's Eye C system and have no LiDAR.
- **Huawei:** The two pricier variants use Huawei's Qiankun ADS 3.0 system, which the article says enables urban NOA (Navigation on Autopilot). Each has one 192-channel LiDAR on the roof.
- **Chip:** The article doesn't mention the chip used in either system.

**Original Bao 5 launch:** Fang Cheng Bao launched the brand on August 16, 2023, and the Bao 5 received its official debut then. The model went on sale November 9, 2023, with the FiPilot smart driving system.

**Sales:**
- In 2024, the Bao 5 sold 48,913 units, or 86.74% of Fang Cheng Bao's 56,388 total deliveries, according to CnEVPost data.
- In January 2025, the Bao 5 sold 3,210 units, out of the brand's 6,219 total deliveries.

I wrote 47 rows to `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-shengyin-Desktop-2026-10-10-EHL-code-Open-Trend-Tracker/3fd7f23b-806c-42e4-a247-3d41a3610973/scratchpad/cn/pairs_byd.json`, sorted by `current_launch` descending (2025-03-05 to 2022-04-10). Every row is NEV.

The shared 200-search web budget ran out partway through. After that I could only fetch known pages and use CnEVPost's own site search. Some dates and figures below were therefore not cross-checked.

**What the rows cover:**
- **Feb 10, 2025 Smart Driving Edition wave (18 rows):** Han EV, Han DM, Qin Plus DM-i, Qin Plus EV, Qin L DM-i, Seal 06 DM-i, Seal 05 DM-i, Song Plus DM-i, Song Plus EV, Song Pro DM-i, Song L DM-i, Song L EV, Sealion 07 EV, Seal 07 DM-i, Yuan Up, Seagull, Dolphin and Tang DM.
- **Feb–Mar 2025, other brands:** Yuan Plus (2025-03-05) and Fangchengbao Bao 5 (2025-02-21).
- **DM 5.0 / 2025 model-year updates in 2024:** Song Plus DM-i, Song Plus EV, Seal EV, Seal DM-i → Seal 07 DM-i, Han EV, Han DM, Song Pro, Tang DM, and Denza D9 (2024-12-27).
- **Feb–Mar 2024 Glory Editions with a concrete added feature:** Han EV, Han DM, Tang DM-i, Dolphin, Seal DM-i and Frigate 07, plus the 2024 Denza D9 (2024-03-06).
- **2023 Champion Editions:** Qin Plus DM-i, Qin Plus EV, Han EV, Han DM-i, Tang DM-i, Song Plus DM-i, Song Plus EV, Song Pro and Yuan Plus.
- **April 2022 Han facelift:** two rows, EV and DM-i/DM-p.

**Doubts:**
1. **Split nameplates.** I gave Han, Tang, Song Plus and Qin Plus separate EV and DM rows, because their launch dates differ. Most per-powertrain sales come from Wikipedia's tables. The Qin Plus split is my own estimate (DM-i about 260k in 2022 and 380k in 2024; EV about 80k and 100k), taken from verified combined totals of about 340k (2022) and 480,025 (2024). Song L DM-i (~145k) and Yuan Up (~155k) are extrapolated from Jan–Nov 2024 figures.
2. **Renamed lines.** Destroyer 05 → Seal 05 DM-i and Seal DM-i → Seal 07 DM-i are both treated as the same line. That may not match how sales tables list them.
3. **Glory/Honor Editions left out.** I dropped the ones that were mainly price cuts or colours: Qin Plus DM-i/EV, Destroyer 05, Song Plus, Song Pro, Seagull, Yuan Plus, Seal EV, Tang EV/DM-p. The Qin Plus and Yuan Plus Glory Editions only added software items (continuous voice, smart power-on). The Han DM-i Glory row only adds DiLink 5.0 and is borderline.
